title: Stilling the mind
hook: yoga is the stilling of the mind's movements (Yoga Sutras 1.2)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ashtanga: Patanjali's eight limbs, starting with how you treat people. Your line was eight limbs. Did you keep the first one, not harming, for a whole ordinary hour? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-four.

The Yoga Sutras don't warm up. The first line is barely a sentence: now, the teaching of yoga. The second line is the definition, and the whole book hangs on it. No poses. No breath. No gods, yet. Just a claim about what's going on behind your eyes, all day, every day: the mind is moving. It flickers from a memory to a worry to a plan, to a song from a commercial, to the memory again. Yoga, the second line says, is what happens when that stills. Today's word is that line.
screen: `LINE ONE: NOW, THE TEACHING OF YOGA.` → `LINE TWO: THE DEFINITION.` → `THE MIND IS MOVING.`

segments.voice: Sutra one point two: yogash chitta vritti nirodhah. Yoga is the stilling of the movements of the mind. Translators reach for different English. Chitta is the mind, or the whole field of awareness. Vritti has been put as movements, fluctuations, modifications, whirls. Nirodha as restraint, cessation, stilling. And then, the next line: when that happens, the seer rests in its own nature. Otherwise, the line after says, the seer takes on the shape of the movements. That's the heart of it. Much of the day, in this picture, a person looks like whatever is moving through them. Angry when the anger moves, anxious when the worry moves. Here's the surprising part. The book lists the kinds of movement, and there are five: right knowledge, error, imagination, sleep and memory. Right knowledge is on the list. So is sleep. The stilling isn't only about clearing out bad thoughts. Even true thoughts are movements. Even the blankness of sleep is one. So how does it happen? Sutra one point twelve gives the answer in two words: practice, and non-attachment. Practice is coming back. Non-attachment is letting go of what pulls you away. And the book adds that practice becomes firm when it's kept up for a long time, without a break, and with care. Nothing quick. One image teachers reach for is a lake. When the wind drops, the surface goes flat, and you can see straight down to the bottom. The water was always clear. It was just moving.
screen: `THE STILLING OF THE MIND'S MOVEMENTS.` · `THE SEER RESTS IN ITS OWN NATURE.` · `FIVE MOVEMENTS, EVEN SLEEP.` · `PRACTICE, AND LETTING GO.` · then, large: `THE WATER WAS ALWAYS CLEAR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit still. Choose a position you can hold without fidgeting, and decide now not to move until the bell. Let the body be the first thing that stills. Then watch the mind move. A memory goes by. A plan. A sound. Don't chase any of it, and don't fight it. Each time you notice you've been carried off, that's the practice: come back to sitting still. If you'd like to go longer when the bell rings, stay for five minutes. The bell holds the time.
Stilling the mind. Patanjali's definition of yoga: the movements of the mind grow still, and the seer rests in its own nature. Today's word.

Your line: stilling. Today, the next time you feel yourself take the shape of a mood, name the movement, worry, memory, plan, and let it pass like wind over water. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-four.

howItsDone: Students of the Yoga Sutras learn sutra 1.2 as the definition of yoga and practice stilling the mind in seated meditation, coming back again and again, with non-attachment to whatever pulls them away.

fork.setup: you sit down and your mind is racing. by sutra 1.12, what stills it?
fork.reveal: practice, the coming back, and non-attachment, letting go of what pulls you away. two words carry the whole method.

original.note: Sanskrit, from Yoga Sutras 1.2: the stilling of the movements of the mind.

trapdoor: what you thought: stilling the mind means making it go blank.
what it means: the movements of the mind settle, and the seer rests in its own nature instead of taking their shape.
what a scholar hears: citta-vritti-nirodhah, sutra 1.2. the book's five kinds of vritti include right knowledge and sleep, and nirodha has been rendered restraint, cessation and stilling.

notes: All Yoga Sutras material paraphrased. Confirm: 1.1 'now, the teaching of yoga'; 1.2 rendering and the range of translations given for chitta, vritti and nirodha.

1.3 and 1.4 (the seer rests in its own nature; otherwise takes the form of the movements); 1.6 five vrittis: pramana, viparyaya, vikalpa, nidra, smriti (rendered right knowledge, error, imagination, sleep, memory); 1.12 abhyasa and vairagya; 1.14 dirgha-kala, nairantarya, satkara.
The lake image is attributed to 'teachers', not to the sutra. Confirm.
Outline practice says five minutes; the app sits for two, so the practice invites staying for five.
